Maria Gottlieb stared at horror at the man sitting on her couch. She’s known he was coming, Menno had told her, but he’d all but barged into her apartment and took a seat on her couch. With a devilish, nigh irresistible smile, he sat there, his arms spread out, a bottle of wine in his hand.

As he noticed her eye, he angled the wine bottle so she could see it.

Correct: a bottle of her favorite wine. He’d remembered.

She could just kill him. If he wasn’t so big. And she so small in comparison. She was tall for a girl, but Steiner was still Steiner.

With that infectious grin on his face, he looked at her. “Care to join me?”

“Fuck you,” she spat.

The words only seemed to amuse him. “Tsk, tsk, tsk, pretty ladies like yourself ought not be so vulgar.”

“You can’t just walk into my life, not again, and pretend that nothing happened!” She crossed her arms. As he looked at her, Maria suddenly felt incredibly conscious of her body. All she was wearing as a tank top and a pair of shorts, whereas he was wearing a black blazer. It looked expensive, custom-tailored.

“You’re right. I had General de Vries set the date up for you.”

“Like I had a choice.”

“You did. Always have. Never didn’t,” he said with more seriousness. “You went your way in life, and I went mine.”

“You left me!” she almost yelled. “I kept in contact with Erik, but even he drifted away from me to work with you. You and your mad ideas!”

“The Iron Dream, you mean,” Steiner insisted. He patted the couch cushion. “So, care for a drink? If you’ve no cups, we can drink from the tap.” He winked.

Maria just stood there. She almost couldn’t believe it. He just didn’t take her seriously. It was like everything was a goddamn joke to Steiner. Yet this was the man everyone worried would one day become Chancellor? Insane!

“I’m trying to be diplomatic, Maria,” he told her, eyeing her up and down. Maria felt a little uncomfortable under his eyes. “Like it or not, the AfD and joining with the DNVP. Together, we are stronger. And we all know why you’re genius PR has failed so far.”

She crossed her arms. “Why?”

“Because you can’t put your heart behind something you don’t believe in,” he said like it was the simplest thing. “You joined the AfD because they’d have you. But at heart, you belong with me, with the DNVP.”

“Bullshit!’ she accused. “Just because we used to be an item doesn’t mean I followed you.”

He just smiled that nigh irresistible smile some more. “As I recall, when we were kids—you, Erik, and I—you almost couldn’t keep yourself away from me. Funny that, the rich girl and the poor boy. Good times, were they not?” He shrugged. “Well, except for mother dying and me having to survive by myself..

“And when I came back, you were a woman in full bloom, and I found you still had a shrine to me in your heart.” He looked like he was enjoying an old memory. Maria knew just exactly what he was picturing. Steiner, fresh from a tour of duty in the special force, came to see her as she starting university. And she had… he had been the only man to… Thinking about it made Maria hate herself.

“By then, you knew for sure of my beliefs. As a little girl, you were there as I came to realize my thoughts were the manifestation of the Iron Dream. Erik adored me for it. And you? Well, I don’t think we need to state how you felt. Your flesh made that clear.”

“Why are you here?” Maria asked him. He meant to state it almost as a command, but it came out weak, girlish.

“Because despite what happened between us, I never disliked you. Our paths diverged, and now they converge again. If that’s not at least someone up above pulling strings, I don’t know what is.” He set the bottle down and stood up. “Maria, I can’t make you work with me. But I’d ask you to. You’re a PR genius; I’ve seen it. You’re a born diplomat. And you do yourself a disservice by not fighting for something you can believe is. Fight with me. Dare to dream the Iron Dream, Maria.”

She wanted to strike him. But at the same time, as she looked into his glacial blue eyes, she couldn’t help but want to. Oh, how badly she wanted to, just like old times.

tl;dr Steiner and Maria used to date way back when (he was her first, hint hint). Now, with the AfD and DNVP merger, he convinces her to work with him like in the old days before he broke her heart.
